questions.topic: PrepLadder · 70.Autoimmune Hepatitis, Primary Biliary Cirrhosis, Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, and Paracetamol Toxicity
questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents to the clinic with fatigue, jaundice, and abdominal discomfort. Lab tests show elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT). Further testing reveals positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and anti-smooth muscle antibodies (ASMA). A liver biopsy demonstrates interface hepatitis with plasma cell infiltration. Given the specific autoantibody profile and the histological findings, which of the following options is associated with the condition and is most relevant to consider in this patient?
